name: Crucible Industries Garrison Rifle GR-5 'Rampart'
description:
The GR-5 Rampart is a heavy-barreled 7.62mm assault rifle designed for static defensive positions — guard towers, checkpoints, and fortified perimeters. The weapon features an integrated mounting clamp that locks into standard defensive position fixtures, providing a stable firing platform without requiring a bipod or sandbag rest. Once mounted, the Rampart's BCI link interfaces with the defensive position's sensor array to provide 360-degree threat detection and automated tracking.

The rifle's heavy barrel profile supports sustained fire rates that would overheat lighter weapons, and a quick-change barrel system allows hot barrels to be swapped in under ten seconds. The magazine well accepts standard 30-round boxes as well as Crucible's proprietary 100-round drum for extended engagements. The weapon is unwieldy for mobile operations — at 5.5 kilograms before mounting hardware, it is firmly in the 'emplaced weapon' category.

Crucible sells the Rampart to settlement defense forces, corporate facility security, and any organization that needs to hold ground. The weapon is frequently encountered at checkpoints across GLMZ, mounted to standardized defensive fixtures and ready to deny passage to anyone unauthorized.
specifications: caliber: 7.62mm caseless effective_range: 700m rate_of_fire: 650 rpm (cyclic) magazine_capacity: 30 rounds (box) / 100 rounds (drum) weight: 5.5 kg (unmounted)
tactical_use: The Rampart is a position defense weapon. Mounted in a prepared position with sensor integration, it provides a single operator with the sustained firepower normally requiring a crew-served weapon. The quick-change barrel ensures continuous fire capability during extended siege scenarios. The 100-round drum magazine allows a full minute of sustained fire without reloading. The weapon's weight and mounting system make it impractical for mobile operations.
cultural_context: The Rampart is the weapon of walls and gates — wherever people draw a line and dare others to cross it. Settlements evaluate their security by counting their Ramparts, and the presence of GR-5s at a checkpoint signals serious defensive intent. In Tier 1-2 communities, a mounted Rampart is often the most powerful weapon available, and the person who operates it holds disproportionate importance in the settlement's defense hierarchy.
story_hooks: A settlement's three Rampart positions have been sabotaged simultaneously — the quick-change barrels were replaced with units that will catastrophically fail after 50 rounds of sustained fire.

A Rampart operator at a disputed checkpoint has been ordered to deny passage to refugees fleeing a corporate conflict zone. The operator's BCI shows women, children, and wounded civilians approaching their firing position.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutish, purpose-built defensive rifle with an oversized barrel profile and integrated mounting hardware. The silhouette is deliberately heavy and anchored — a weapon meant to stay planted. Angular receiver geometry suggests industrial manufacturing rather than ergonomic refinement. The front-mounted clamp assembly protrudes like a mechanical mandible, giving it an almost skeletal appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: 1020mm overall length, 95mm width (at mounting clamp), 280mm height (including integrated clamp). Heavy 260mm barrel with visible heat vanes running its length.
physical_description.weight_description: Decidedly hefty — 5.5kg of pure inertia before mounting hardware. Feels like shouldering a concrete-filled tube. The weight is front-heavy, pulling the muzzle down naturally.
physical_description.primary_material: Forged steel receiver with carbon-composite furniture. The barrel is chrome-molybdenum with longitudinal cooling fins. Mounting clamp is hardened steel with precision-machined locking teeth.
physical_description.finish: Matte electroless nickel on steel components with a dull graphite-gray anodize on composite surfaces. The heavy barrel shows selective polishing marks where quick-change locking lugs engage.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with charcoal polymer accents. The mounting clamp features faded Crucible Industries stenciling in industrial white.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with aggressive horizontal ridges cut into the surface. Designed for gloved hands — unforgiving to bare skin. The charging handle is knurled steel, cold and clinical.
distinctive_features: Longitudinal cooling fins running the entire barrel length — visible heat dissipation geometry
Integrated mechanical mounting clamp with precision locking teeth and indicator groove
Quick-change barrel lug assembly with numbered heat marks (1-4) showing barrel swap positions
Recessed BCI interface port on the left receiver — a silver circle embedded flush with the polymer
100-round drum magazine well with distinctly reinforced shoulder — overbuilt for sustained fire
Top-mounted Picatinny rail with factory-installed sensor bracket pads (dimpled for optical alignment)
Ejection port surrounded by heat-scarring — carbon buildup and burnished marks from years of checkpoint duty
Serial plate stamped KSPL-GR5-████ below the receiver (obscured designation)
Crucible Industries logo: a stylized furnace symbol, repeated on barrel shroud and magazine well
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Kill-Switch Pathogen Lab (KSPL) stamp on the dust cover. Crucible Industries furnace logo appears on the barrel shroud and upper receiver. Patent notation (faded) on the mounting clamp: 'MECH LOCK 2218'. Serial number plate recessed below the receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but heavily used. The barrel shows heat-bluing and burnish marks from frequent quick-changes. The mounting clamp has shallow gouges and wear-polishing from countless installations. The ejection port shows carbon buildup and smell of burnt propellant. Checkpoint operators keep these weapons functional but not pristine — they're tools, not showpieces.
